messages:
maya: Heads-up — after today's canary the MetricsPanel sparklines are timing out on heavy dashboards in eu1. LCP up, lots of frozen paint. Anyone else seeing this?
liam: seeing similar in prod-canary, widgets using TileLoader hang around 2-3s longer.
junaid: metrics — heatmap of requests shows a spike in requests to /api/metrics/tile due to prefetch ramp yesterday. could be kv-cache miss storm.
sophia: logs show a lot of 522 timeouts from vendor-embed when charts request remote glyphs, but majority are internal render stalls.
deploy-bot: Canary deployed build sha: abc123 -> eu1 at 1749123400 (strategy: 10% traffic).
maya: @liam can you grab a flame and post a short profile? high-level first.
liam: quick flame: main-thread blocked ~60% on readTile()/deserialize, chunk parsing + JSON.parse hotspots. attaching snippet: ```js
// approx
const tiles = await Promise.all(keys.map(k => kv.get(k)));
const parsed = tiles.map(t => JSON.parse(t));
```
junaid: that map+JSON.parse on UI thread is rough. we should defer parse to worker or use binary proto. Also kv cache eviction might be thrashing because prefix hints changed in rollout.
sophia: telemetry sampling was bumped to 100% for canary to get coverage, that may be adding overhead on main path — we instrument at parse boundaries.
maya: ah — the telemetry change was in PR #4123 (rollout telemetry/sample-rate). I thought we only instrumented timers, but looks like we added synchronous serialization for each tile event.
liam: suggestion: revert the sampling bump or make it async/write-to-queue. immediate mitigation: throttle prefetch concurrency from 32 -> 8.
junaid: +1. also enable KV cache affinity so hot keys stay local to shard. config is in services/prefetch/config.yaml -> prefetch: concurrency. we can patch via infra flag.
ops-bot: Alert: console-ui CPU utilization in eu1 > 80% for 5m. Incident created: INCIDENT-2024-78.
maya: I'll do the concurrency patch now, rolling patch to canary. @deploy-bot can you pause the canary ramp to 0% while we test?
deploy-bot: Canary ramp paused by maya at 1749123520.
liam: quick patch diff (local): ```diff
- concurrency: 32
+ concurrency: 8
```
liam: also opening a PR to move JSON.parse off main thread (WIP) — https://git.internal/r/redwood/console/pull/4678
sophia: for longer term, we should avoid full-tile JSON blobs. proto + structured clone to worker, or keep KV as binary.
junaid: agree. planning follow-up EPIC: TILE-OPT (breakdown: serialization, kv-sharding, prefetch-policy).
maya: after throttle applied, can everyone watch the canary metrics for 10m and report back?
liam: early numbers: LCP back down ~700ms (from ~1.8s). still some edge spikes but much better.
sophia: telemetry ingestion dropped as well (expected). I'll revert the 100% sampling patch in the canary branch after we stabilize.
maya: sweet. assign follow-ups: @liam -> worker-parse PR, @junaid -> kv affinity config, @sophia -> revert telemetry sampling. I'll keep incident updated.
ops-bot: INCIDENT-2024-78 status: mitigated (throttle applied) at 1749123700.
maya: closing thread for now, we'll track TILE-OPT in the sprint board. thanks all :raised_hands:
